decisions.choice: Hybrid: a stored Toman sell price per price version (new table ai_sell_prices), re-priced automatically, plus a per-call floor guard. `ai:reprice` runs hourly at :10, after fx:dollar. It creates a new version in three cases: (1) the live USD rate rises at least up_band above the version's rate, where up_band = min(3%, margin/2); (2) the rate falls at least 5% below it and the version is at least 24 h old; (3) immediately, when the margin, fee, cost row or override changes. At reserve time a floor guard checks the published price against the live rate. If the price would keep less than a quarter of the margin, it re-prices synchronously (reason fx_floor) and that call is priced at the new version. Each call snapshots the sell-version ids, S_u and R_call, and settles at the snapshotted price even if a new version appears mid-call.
decisions.why: Growth: a Toman price per 1M tokens that stays unchanged for days in calm FX can be published on /ai, compared with competitors and cited by search. Reproducibility: resolveAt plus snapshots rebuild any charge exactly. Red line: the band limits how much margin FX can erode between hourly runs, and the floor guard catches jumps inside an hour, so no call is priced below cost.

decisions.choice: The rate comes from a new CloudPricing::usdToToman(), in this order: pricing_usd_rate_override (now validated to the 20k–5M range; a value more than 15% away from the last live rate needs a confirm checkbox) → ExchangeRate::current('USD') (the cache, falling back to lastKnown up to 48 h old) → null. EUR cost rows use eurToToman(). The hot path never scrapes. Up to 6 h old: normal. 6–48 h old: the floor guard and repricing assume the rate is 3% higher (stale buffer) and an admin alert fires. Unknown (null): new calls get 503 pricing_unavailable, and /ai shows 'temporarily unavailable' instead of guessed prices. Our real cost of buying USD is modelled as pricing_fx_fee_pct_deepinfra, not as a second FX source.
decisions.why: The scraper already feeds domains and cloud pricing. When it fails, the owner can keep selling by setting an override. Selling on a rate more than 48 h old risks a sale below cost, so it is refused.

decisions.choice: The owner types a global ai_margin_pct: validated strictly >0 and ≤500, with no other floor, matching his cloud rule 'my margin is the number I type'. There is a per-provider FX fee, pricing_fx_fee_pct_{slug} (0–25, deepinfra added to the FIELDS whitelist), and an optional per-model margin override, ai_models.margin_bp (also >0). The order is cost × (1+fee) × (1+margin), rounding up at each step. There are no per-customer prices at launch: forCustomer stays null until B16 is fixed.
decisions.why: The owner keeps pricing as a competitive tool: a thin margin on flagship models, more on niche ones. Margin >0 plus the real fee plus rounding up makes net revenue strictly greater than cost on every call. A margin of 0 is the only way to break the red line, so it is the only value refused.

decisions.choice: (a) A new AiReservations::settleActual: one transition writes one credit_ledger row = usage × the snapshotted sell prices + VAT, and the rest of the hold disappears in the same transaction. Cached tokens: DeepInfra reports prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, so cached input is billed as its own unit from its own cost row; without a cached cost row it is billed at the input price (never below cost). Reasoning tokens are inside completion_tokens and billed at the output price; they are recorded separately for display only. Usage missing or invalid: charge the hold as a cap (owner decision), with usage_source=cap and needs_review=1. Usage above the hold: charge the actual amount (owner: never absorb), with a bounded overdraft recorded in overdraft_irt. Output cannot exceed the hold because max_tokens is forced.
decisions.why: The customer pays exactly what the provider's usage says at the published price, so the response `usage` matches the debit, which builds trust. One ledger row per call keeps statements clean (no refund noise). The cap and overdraft rules follow the owner's 'charge real cost, never absorb'.

decisions.choice: Published prices are rounded up to whole Toman per 1M tokens, then up to 3 significant digits. Each call is one ceilDiv over the whole sum, to whole Toman (minimum 1 Toman when tokens > 0). VAT is a separate ceilDiv. The µ-currency per-unit ceil (chargeMicros) is no longer used to charge, so nothing is rounded twice. There is no per-request minimum fee, and the IRT rounding_step is never applied per call. The hold uses the same formula.
decisions.why: The bias is at most 1 Toman per call, about $0.00001, and always upward. The published number is exactly the multiplier the customer can check against their usage. Three significant digits keep the list readable and stop small recomputations from creating new versions.

decisions.choice:
SSE ships at launch (owner decision, launch blocker). Rejecting stream would break the OpenAI Python/Node SDKs with stream=True, the Vercel AI SDK streamText, LangChain .stream(), Open WebUI, LibreChat, Cursor, Continue and most chat UIs. It would also push long answers into proxy and gateway timeouts. Design:
- Gates and the hold are done before any header is sent, so errors before the first byte are normal JSON errors.
- The upstream is called with stream:true and stream_options.include_usage=true, and each SSE event is relayed with model and id rewritten.
- Usage is taken from whichever chunk carries it. DeepInfra puts it on the final finish_reason chunk before [DONE] (docs.deepinfra.com/chat/streaming); a separate usage-only chunk is also accepted.
- If the client disconnects, ignore_user_abort(true): the upstream is drained up to the wall cap and actual usage is charged.
- A failure mid-stream sends an SSE `data: {"error":{...}}` event and the cap policy applies.
decisions.why: Most real clients stream. Streaming is also the only way long generations survive the Apache Timeout. The provider bills the full generation even when our client leaves, so draining and charging actual usage is both exact and no-loss.

decisions.choice:
Owner policy, implemented as follows:
- Before the request body is sent (validation, gates, connect, DNS or TLS failure): release, no charge, and the idempotency key is freed.
- Provider answered non-2xx: release, no charge.
- Request sent but no usable usage (read timeout, non-JSON or invalid 2xx, stream cut before usage, worker crash found by the reconciler): charge the hold (cap), flag needs_review, and respond with x-should-retry:false.
- Settle DB failure after success: retry the transaction 3× on 1213/1205/40001; if it still fails, return 200 with the body anyway. The row becomes settle_failed and the reconciler settles it within 5 min from the stored usage.
- A late settle past expires_at is allowed and may overdraw the wallet. The account then gets 402 until it is topped up.
- We never return a 5xx after upstream success.
decisions.why: SDKs retry 5xx and 409 automatically. A 500 after a successful call makes the SDK buy the same answer twice, which is the most expensive trust failure. The owner ruled out absorbing costs, and the review flag gives the admin a one-click refund path when the cap was unfair.

decisions.choice:
The Idempotency-Key is optional, at most 80 printable ASCII characters (otherwise 400). It is bound to the sha256 of the canonical request body (JSON with sorted keys, model included):
- Same key, same hash, completed: replay the stored answer. Non-stream gets the JSON; stream gets a synthesized single-delta SSE plus usage plus [DONE]. Header idempotent-replayed:true, no upstream call, no charge.
- Same key, same hash, in flight: 409 request_in_progress, which SDKs retry with backoff.
- Same key, different hash: 400 idempotency_key_reused.
- Released or failed without charge: the key is freed. On release it is moved from ai_reservations.idempotency_key to released_key so the unique index lets a retry through.
- Replay window 24 h. Responses are stored only for keyed requests, encrypted, pruned after 24 h.
decisions.why: This is the standard client retry contract (Stripe/OpenAI style). It fixes B12's permanent 409 and the replay of the wrong prompt. The body is kept only as long as the replay needs it.

decisions.choice: One IRT wallet; € is display only, for en/tr. The price list shows € per 1M tokens = S_u ÷ cloud_eur_rate(), the same live rate that converts their € top-ups, rounded up to 3 significant digits (e.g. €0.281). History and statements use each request's eur_rate_irt snapshot. There is no EUR wallet and no € receipts; statements are in Toman with a € equivalent. If the EUR rate is missing, Toman is shown, never a guessed €.
decisions.why: This matches the existing site pattern (cloud_price and the topup conversion), so what an en/tr customer sees is what their wallet buys. A second wallet would split balances and conflict with the owner's one-wallet requirement.

decisions.choice: VAT is added on top of the ex-VAT published price (owner decision). vat_bp is snapshotted per call: TaxRate::resolve('IR', null, 'ai') (a new tax_rates row, rate_bp 1000) for VAT-liable customers, 0 otherwise. The default liability rule is customers.locale='fa', matching Product::effectiveTaxPercent; the owner must confirm (question 1). Each call debits net+VAT as one credit_ledger row, reason ai_usage. BusinessLedger gets a daily rollup per provider (ai_usage_daily): revenue (category ai) = Σnet, tax_collected (category ai) = Σtax, expense (category ai_upstream) = the daily ceiling of Σcost_utoman ÷ 1e6. Cost is accrued daily from usage and reconciled monthly against the DeepInfra invoice. DeepInfra top-ups are never also booked as an expense.
decisions.why: The daily rollup keeps the unique (source_type, source_id, kind) idempotency and avoids flooding the ledger. Accruing cost from the same rows as revenue makes margin auditable per day and per model.

decisions.choice: Keep it separate. M5 does not touch hourly cloud or BusinessReport's hourly side block. The ai_usage_daily plus recordAiDay pattern is written generically so a follow-up task can apply it to hourly cloud and remove the side block in the same change.
decisions.why: Changing hourly reporting in the same per-file deploy risks double counting and adds more prod files. AI starts with zero history, so there is nothing to reconcile.

decisions.choice:
Budgets are hard-enforced at reserve, inside the customer lock:
- Project: Σcharged_irt settled in the window + Σ held by the project + the new hold must be ≤ monthly_budget_irt (VAT-inclusive).
- Token: the token's own daily_spend_cap_irt, only if explicitly set. The reseller and config fallbacks of dailySpendCap() are not used for AI.
- The Toman amount is stored for everyone. en/tr users enter €, which is converted at save and displayed as €.
- The window is computed on read in Asia/Tehran from budget_reset_day. The budget_window_stale gate and month-end lockout are removed, and the create form infers monthly when a budget is given.
- Exceeding it gives 402 budget_exceeded with x-should-retry:false. Email/Bale alerts go out once per window at 80% and 100%.
decisions.why: The budget chip is a promise to the customer, and for API keys leaked into client apps it is the main protection. Hard enforcement costs one indexed SUM inside a lock we already hold.

decisions.choice: Cost rows stay in ai_model_unit_prices (provider list price, USD or EUR only). Sell versions in ai_sell_prices are computed by formula. An optional manual sell override per model and unit (e.g. a round marketing price) is accepted only if it is at or above the formula floor at the current FX with margin >0. If FX later makes an override below cost, the floor guard supersedes it and alerts.
decisions.why: One margin setting moves every price automatically. Marketing keeps control of headline prices, and no manual row can break the red line.

decisions.choice: Prompts are never stored (only request_hash). Response bodies are kept only for keyed requests, encrypted in a new ai_calls.response_enc column (MariaDB JSON columns reject ciphertext), with a 24 h TTL. Metadata (tokens, money, snapshots) is kept 24 months as a financial record. White-labelling: `model` is rewritten to our slug, `id` becomes chatcmpl-sn<ULID>, and usage.estimated_cost and provider-only fields are stripped. Provider headers are never relayed. ToS and privacy updates disclose a US sub-processor (owner question 6).
decisions.why: This keeps us out of GDPR and customer-confidentiality exposure, prevents customers routing around us to DeepInfra, and still makes replay possible.

decisions.choice: Balance-aware max_tokens: when the client omits max_tokens and the default hold exceeds the available balance, the forwarded max_tokens is lowered to what the balance affords. The minimum is 256 tokens, below which the answer is 402. The response may then end with finish_reason=length, and the docs say so.

decisions.why: The owner requires usage visibility. A product-grade dashboard is the retention surface, and it is where low-balance and budget alerts link.

decisions.choice:

decisions.why: Developers can match each charge to its request. SDKs and tools parse the standard envelope, and extra fields are ignored by OpenAI SDK models.

settlement_algorithm:
All money is integer. ceilDiv(a,b) = ⌈a/b⌉ for a ≥ 0. MicroMath::mulDivCeil(a,b,d) = intdiv(a,d)·b + ceilDiv((a mod d)·b, d). It is exact, and it throws MoneyOverflow (mapped to 503 not_priced, never a TypeError; fixes B18) if (d−1)·b or intdiv(a,d)·b would exceed PHP_INT_MAX. S_u = snapshotted sell price in Toman per 1M tokens. V = vat_bp.

RESERVE (AiCaller::handle, before any HTTP):
1. Gates, in order:
   - sales gate (ai_sales_open or beta list)
   - admission (AiAdmission; project_missing is checked before can(); use_count, last_used_at and last_used_ip are written only after all gates)
   - model active, isSellable(), provider.isAgreedTo() and resale_allowed, category=chat
   - driver resolvable
2. AiPayload::normalize:
   - messages must be a non-empty array
   - n ∈ {absent, 1}, else 400 unsupported_parameter
   - image, audio and file content parts give 400 unsupported_content; text array parts are counted
   - max_completion_tokens is mapped to max_tokens
   - stream is a bool
   - tools, tool_choice and response_format pass through
3. Input estimate:
   - T_in_hold = min(model.context_tokens ?: ∞, ceilDiv(strlen(json_encode({messages,tools,tool_choice,response_format}, UNESCAPED_UNICODE)), model.hold_bytes_per_token = 2) + 4·count(messages) + 16).
   - Bytes/2 is deliberately conservative: it about doubles English and covers Persian and CJK.
4. Output cap:
   - T_out = max(1, min(requested ?? model.default_max_output_tokens ?? model_cap, model_cap)), with model_cap = max_output_tokens ?: 4096.
   - The forwarded payload.max_tokens is forced to T_out (B6).
5. Prices and FX:
   - Resolve the active sell versions S_in, S_out, S_cached (S_cached := S_in when absent) and cost rows c_in, c_out, c_cached.
   - Take FxQuote R_call (the stale buffer applies when older than 6 h; unknown gives 503 pricing_unavailable).
   - Floor guard: if any S_u < floor_u(R_call), re-price synchronously under a lock on the ai_models row (outside the customer lock) and use the new version.
6. Hold:
   - hold_net = ceilDiv(S_in·T_in_hold + S_out·T_out, 1e6) (rounded up)
   - hold = hold_net + ceilDiv(hold_net·V, 10000) (rounded up)
   - V is snapshotted from the customer's VAT liability.
   - Balance-aware (P3): only when the client omitted max_tokens and hold > available. Set cap_net = ⌊(available−1)·10000/(10000+V)⌋ and T_out' = ⌊(cap_net·1e6 − S_in·T_in_hold)/S_out⌋. If T_out' ≥ 256, set T_out = T_out' and recompute the hold; otherwise answer 402.
7. One DB transaction (the existing reserve lock order: the customer row FOR UPDATE):
   - Idempotency: same key and hash settled gives a replay; same key in flight gives 409; different hash gives 400. The key is re-checked under the lock, fixing the 402-instead-of-duplicate case.
   - Concurrency: holding reservations must be below the project, customer and global limits (429).
   - Budget: project Σcharged_irt with settled_at in the Tehran window + Σ project holds + hold ≤ monthly_budget_irt. Token: its explicit daily_spend_cap_irt, same rule over the Tehran day. Violation gives 402 budget_exceeded.
   - Funds: Wallet::availableOf ≥ hold, else 402 insufficient_funds.
   - Insert ai_reservations: amount_irt = hold (Toman), project, token, request_hash, expires_at = now + budget + 120 s (budget: 240 s non-stream, 600 s stream).
   - Insert ai_requests with status reserved and every snapshot: S_u and their ids, c_u, R_call, fee_bp, margin_bp, V, eur_rate, T_in_hold, T_out, reserved_irt = hold.
8. UPDATE ai_requests SET status='sent', upstream_sent_at=now() just before the request body is written (on_stats or pretransfer), so the reconciler can tell 'never sent' from 'sent'.

SETTLE (after upstream, or from the reconciler):
9. Read usage (non-stream: body.usage; stream: the chunk carrying usage):
   - P = prompt_tokens, C = completion_tokens, K = prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens ?? 0, Z = completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens ?? 0 (display only).
   - They are valid if all are ints ≥ 0, K ≤ P and P+C > 0.
   - Persist P/K/C/Z and upstream_request_id at once in a small UPDATE, before the money transaction, so a crash after this point still settles actual usage.
10. Charge:
    - With valid usage (usage_source = provider): net = max(1, ceilDiv(S_in·(P−K) + S_cached·K + S_out·C, 1e6)) (rounded up once per call); tax = ceilDiv(net·V, 10000) (rounded up); charged = net + tax.
    - Invalid or missing usage (usage_source = cap, needs_review = 1): net = hold_net, tax = hold − hold_net, charged = hold.
11. Cost:
    - cost_pusd = c_in·(P−K) + c_cached·K + c_out·C (exact). For a cap charge, the token counts are T_in_hold and T_out.
    - cost_utoman = mulDivCeil(ceilDiv(cost_pusd, 1e6)·R_call, 10000+fee_bp, 10000) (rounded up = conservative).
    - Invariant: net·1e6 > cost_utoman. If it is violated, set below_floor = 1, raise ErrorTracker 'ai_below_floor', and queue ai:reprice for the model. The published price is still charged; it is never raised after the fact.
12. AiReservations::settleActual(reservation, charged, request) in a transaction:
    - Lock the customer, then the reservation. Settled already: return it, no second debit. Released: error. Pending: accepted even past expires_at, because the originating request or the reconciler owns it.
    - Wallet::settleDebit(customer, 'IRT', charged, 'ai_usage', source = AiRequest, excludingReservationId = r.id, allowOverdraft = true) writes exactly one credit_ledger row of −charged. If balance − other holds − charged < 0 it still writes and records overdraft_irt = the shortfall.
    - The reservation gets status settled, charged_irt and ledger_entry_id.
    - ai_requests gets status settled, charged_net_irt, tax_irt, charged_irt, cost_pusd, cost_utoman, credit_ledger_id, settled_at, and ledger_day = the Tehran date of settled_at.
    - The unused part of the hold vanishes in the same commit; no refund row.
    - The transaction is retried 3× (50/150/400 ms) on MySQL 1213, 1205 or SQLSTATE 40001. After that the row becomes settle_failed and the client still gets 200.
13. Usage greater than the hold: charged > hold is allowed (never absorb). overage = charged − hold is logged as a calibration signal. Output cannot overrun because max_tokens is forced, so an overrun only comes from input tokenization and is small.
14. Release (no charge): used when the request body was never sent or the provider answered non-2xx. The transaction sets the reservation to released and moves idempotency_key to released_key, and sets ai_requests to status failed with error_code.

RECONCILER (ai:reconcile every 5 min, withoutOverlapping). It handles ai_requests in reserved, sent, streaming or settle_failed whose reservation is pending and either past expires_at or settle_failed for more than 60 s:
- upstream_sent_at null → release
- usage persisted → settleActual with actual usage
- otherwise → cap charge with needs_review
Then expirePending runs for legacy rows. Every action is idempotent and logged.

Tehran-day rule: ledger_day is fixed at settlement time, so a late settle lands on the day it happened and never on a day that is already posted.
pricing_formula:
Inputs (all integers):
- c_u = ai_model_unit_prices.price_micro_units: µ of the cost currency per 1M tokens, for u ∈ {input, cached_input, output}. The currency must be USD or EUR; IRR and IRT are refused (B17). For non-token billing units the divisor comes from the billing unit, not a fixed 1e6 (B11).
- R = Toman per 1 unit of cost currency, from FxQuote.
- F = 10000 + fee_bp, where fee_bp = pricing_fx_fee_pct_{provider}×100 (0–2500).
- M = 10000 + margin_bp, where margin_bp = ai_models.margin_bp ?? ai_margin_pct×100 (1–50000).

SELL PRICE VERSION (AiPricing::sellPerMillion, stored as ai_sell_prices.sell_irt_per_unit, Toman per 1M tokens; every step rounds UP):
- a = c_u·R (µToman per 1M; guarded)
- b = mulDivCeil(a, F, 10000) (adds the FX/transfer fee)
- d = mulDivCeil(b, M, 10000) (adds the margin)
- e = ceilDiv(d, 1_000_000) (whole Toman per 1M = formula_irt_per_unit)
- S_u = ceilSig(e, 3) (published and charged; 30,891 → 30,900; 3,708 → 3,710)

Worked example: c_in = 250,000 ($0.25/1M), c_out = 750,000, R = 100,000, fee 3%, margin 20%.
- S_in = 30,900 Toman/1M; S_out = 92,700 Toman/1M.
- A cached cost of 25,000 gives S_cached = 3,090. Without a cached cost row, S_cached = S_in.

PER-CALL CHARGE (P = prompt, K = cached ≤ P, C = completion including reasoning):
- net = max(1, ceilDiv(S_in·(P−K) + S_cached·K + S_out·C, 1_000_000))
- tax = ceilDiv(net·vat_bp, 10000): 1000 bp for VAT-liable customers, added ON TOP per the owner
- charged = net + tax
- Example: P = 1000, K = 0, C = 50 gives net = ⌈35.535⌉ = 36, tax = 4, charged = 40 Toman.

COST SNAPSHOT (R_call = the rate at reserve):
- cost_pusd = c_in·(P−K) + c_cached·K + c_out·C (exact)
- cost_utoman = mulDivCeil(ceilDiv(cost_pusd, 1e6)·R_call, F, 10000)
- Example: 287,500,000 pUSD → 288 µUSD → 29,664,000 µToman = 29.66 Toman, against a net of 36. The call is about 21% above cost.

RED LINE:
- Per call: net·1e6 > cost_utoman. This is guaranteed while R_call ≤ R_version·M/10000, because margin > 0 and every step rounds up.
- Floor guard at reserve: floor_u(R) = ceilDiv(mulDivCeil(mulDivCeil(c_u·R, F, 10000), 10000+g, 10000), 1e6), where g = max(50, margin_bp/4) and R includes the stale buffer when the rate is 6–48 h old. If S_u < floor_u(R_call), re-price synchronously at R_call (reason fx_floor).
- Manual overrides must satisfy S ≥ floor_u(R_now) when saved.

REPRICE BANDS (ai:reprice hourly at :10, plus immediately on a margin, fee, cost or override change):
- New version if R_live ≥ R_version·(10000+up_bp)/10000, with up_bp = setting or min(300, margin_bp/2).
- Or if R_live ≤ R_version·(10000−down_bp)/10000 (down_bp 500) and the version is at least 24 h old.
- A recomputation that gives the same S_u after 3 significant digits creates no version. That keeps the public list stable.

EUR DISPLAY (en/tr only, display):
- Price list: €/1M = ceilSig3(S_u ÷ cloud_eur_rate()) with ≥4 decimals kept (e.g. €0.281). This is the same live rate that converts € top-ups.
- Spend history: charged_irt ÷ the row's eur_rate_irt, with cloud_hourly_price precision.
- If the EUR rate is missing, Toman is shown.
- /v1/models exposes IRT, with an eur_approx field.
failure_policy:
TIMEOUTS:
- Connect: 5 s.
- Non-stream total: 240 s. It must stay below Apache Timeout (verify it is 300 s on the server).
- Stream: 60 s idle between chunks, 600 s wall.
- Reservation TTL: budget + 120 s.
- Reconciler: every 5 min.
- set_time_limit is only called on the stream path and never under runningUnitTests(), because Windows phpunit exits mid-run.

The driver classifies each failure. Connect-phase failures (connect_timeout, cURL 6/7/35/60, TLS) are not_sent. Anything after the body was written is sent (on_stats: pretransfer > 0 and request size > 0).

A) Before send: no charge. The reservation is released and the idempotency key freed.
- 400 invalid_payload / unsupported_parameter / unsupported_content
- 401 invalid_api_key
- 403 permission (ip_not_allowed, insufficient_scope, project_inactive, account_inactive)
- 402 insufficient_funds / budget_exceeded, with x-should-retry:false
- 429 rate_limited / concurrency_limit, with Retry-After
- 503 service_not_open / pricing_unavailable / model_unavailable / provider_not_live / not_priced
- 502 upstream_unreachable on connect failure (retryable)

B) Provider answered non-2xx: no charge (the provider does not bill failed requests), release.
- provider 400 → 400 invalid_request_error; context_length_exceeded is detected and passed as that code
- provider 401/403 → 503 provider_auth, plus an admin alert (our misconfiguration)
- provider 404 → 503 model_unavailable
- provider 429 → 503 upstream_overloaded, Retry-After 5
- provider 5xx → 502 upstream_error (retryable)

C) Sent, but no usable usage: charge the hold as the cap (owner: 'charge up to the reservation cap, never absorb'), with usage_source=cap and needs_review=1. It shows in the admin review queue with one-click refund, and to the customer as 'charged at hold'. Cases:
- read timeout: 504 upstream_timeout
- 2xx with a non-JSON or invalid body: 502 upstream_bad_response
- stream cut before the usage chunk: an SSE error event, then close
- PHP crash after send: found by the reconciler

All of these carry x-should-retry:false, because a retry would pay twice.

D) Success, but the settle DB transaction fails: retry 3× on deadlock or lock wait. If that fails, still return 200 with the body. The row becomes settle_failed, the hold keeps the funds until expires_at, and the reconciler settles actual usage (a late settle is allowed and may overdraw). We never return a 5xx after upstream success, because SDKs auto-retry 5xx and 409.

E) Client disconnects mid-stream: ignore_user_abort(true). Keep draining the upstream up to the wall cap, then settle actual usage. If the wall cap is hit, abort and apply C.

F) Usage exceeds the hold: charge the actual amount with an overdraft. The account then gets 402 until it is topped up. overdraft_irt is recorded and alerted.

G) FX older than 48 h, or the override is missing: stop new calls (503 pricing_unavailable, retryable) and raise an admin alert. Calls already in flight settle at their snapshot.

KILL SWITCHES: ai_sales_open, provider.live_calls_enabled / commercial_enabled, model.status.

ALERTS (ErrorTracker plus Bale): below_floor > 0, cap charges > 5/hour, any overdraft, settle_failed older than 10 min, FX stale, reconcile variance > 2%.

owner_questions: VAT for foreign customers: should AI usage by en/tr customers (shown in €, wallet funded from € top-ups) carry 0% Iranian VAT? And what should mark a customer as non-Iranian: the portal language (my default: anything other than Persian means 0%), the phone country code, or a country the customer declares?

Tax invoices: for the مودیان system, does AI usage need a formal tax invoice, for example one consolidated invoice per customer per month? Or is a monthly usage statement enough (net, 10% VAT, total, shown in the portal)?

Accounting (please confirm with your accountant): the system will record DeepInfra cost every day, from real usage, as an 'ai_upstream' expense. That means your DeepInfra top-ups must be recorded as prepaid money, not as an expense, or the cost is counted twice. Is that right? And do payments made from your personal account need a reimbursement document?

Launch numbers: what AI margin % do you want? And what does it really cost you, in %, to put $1 into DeepInfra (exchange spread, card or transfer fee, any foreign VAT)? That figure becomes pricing_fx_fee_pct_deepinfra.

Overspend: rarely, the real cost of a request can be a little higher than the amount we held, because input token counts are estimated. Your rule says 'never absorb', so the customer would pay the real amount and their wallet could go slightly negative. AI calls would then be blocked until they top up, and the next top-up covers the gap. Do you accept this?

Resale and legal: DeepInfra is a US company and we have no signed reseller agreement. Do you accept the risk of reselling under their standard terms to Iranian customers, including possible account closure, and allow me to mark the provider 'agreement: signed / resale allowed' so sales can open? Do you also approve updating the terms of service and privacy policy to say prompts are processed by a US provider and to add AI acceptable-use rules?
Growth budget: should new AI customers get free starter credit? If yes, how much, and on what condition (e.g. verified phone or KYC)?

Price changes: are you OK with the published Toman prices changing automatically when the dollar rises 3% or more (at once) or falls 5% or more (at most once a day)? Should customers get an email when prices change?
risks: Single provider: DeepInfra is a US company selling to Iranian residents, so the account can be closed and every model goes dark at once. Mitigation: the driver is OpenAI-compatible, so a second provider is only data (a new provider row plus model rows). Keep the prepaid balance small and plan a second provider in the post-launch backlog.

Apache and PHP-FPM on cPanel may buffer SSE: mod_deflate or mod_proxy_fcgi can deliver all chunks at the end. The client still gets a correct answer but no live streaming. Mitigation: the stream probe gates the launch; .htaccess no-gzip; flushpackets through a WHM include if needed.

Long streams hold PHP-FPM workers and could take the website down. Mitigation: a separate FPM pool on api.servernet.cloud, a global concurrency cap below max_children, and per-customer and per-project concurrency limits.

The Iranian rial can jump sharply within an hour. The floor guard re-prices synchronously and a call in flight settles at its snapshot, so the worst case is one call priced at the pre-jump rate while still keeping a quarter of the margin. If the FX scraper is down for more than 48 h, sales stop unless the owner sets an override.

Input tokens can be underestimated (Persian, CJK or long tool schemas), which causes small overdrafts. Mitigation: the bytes/2 estimate plus overhead, an overdraft alert, and later calibrating hold_bytes_per_token per model from stored prompt_tokens.

Charging the hold when usage is missing will cause customer complaints, especially on read timeouts for non-stream calls. Mitigation: the needs_review queue with one-click refund, the usage source shown in the portal, and internal upstream streaming in the post-launch backlog.

SDK retry behaviour: OpenAI SDKs retry 409, 429 and 5xx. Any code path that returns 5xx after a charge makes the customer pay twice. Mitigation: we never return a 5xx after upstream success, and x-should-retry:false goes on every error where money was charged. Tests pin both.

Prod drift and per-file deploys: a partial file set can silently leave features unshipped or broken, as the ai_calls half-build did. Mitigation: exact file lists, the guarded repair migration, counting Schedule::command before and after, lang files key by key, Route::has guards and an OPcache reset for new route names.

MariaDB DDL is not transactional: a migration that fails midway leaves partial schema. Mitigation: every M5 migration guards each step (hasColumn, hasIndex, hasForeignKey), creates no FK before its parent table, and the owner runs them one --path at a time.
Integer overflow: PHP silently turns an int overflow into a float. Mitigation: mulDivCeil guards, explicit bounds (c ≤ 1e9 µ, R ≤ 5e6, fee ≤ 25%, margin ≤ 500%) and a property test at the bounds.

Tax exposure: collecting 10% VAT on AI adds to VAT that is collected but not filed (per the tax-posture note). The ledger makes it visible, and the owner should settle past periods with an accountant before scaling sales.

Two DeepInfra usage fields are unverified: cached_tokens is documented in DeepInfra's prompt-caching docs but not yet seen in a live response, and estimated_cost is unconfirmed. Verify both in one beta call. If cached_tokens is absent, charge cached tokens as normal input, which is still no loss.

SEO: per-model pages with templated text risk being judged thin or duplicate content. Each listed model needs unique page JSON before it is listed, and the daily content engine should link to the model pages.
PageCache or other middleware reading getContent() on /v1 GETs could cache /v1/models or break a streamed response. /v1 is excluded explicitly and a test covers it.

Tests on Windows: set_time_limit in the stream path can end a phpunit run early while it still exits 0. The stream path skips set_time_limit under runningUnitTests(), and the full suite runs in the background.
